analysis:
Documentation-only change to docs/provider/cli-reference.md: a date bump, a new paragraph (head lines ~926-932) describing drain behavior with the coordinator connection down, and a rewrite of `status`/`doctor` text about enabled_models and Autopilot. The supplied units are BASE text only, covering lines 1-805, and the changed hunks fall at base lines ~923, 991-995 and beyond, so the changed lines are outside what I could inspect. I reviewed the surrounding base text, which describes logout, revocation, drain and cache settings. Nothing there changes code, controls or defaults.

Relevant threat context is A-008, T-053 and T-041, but nothing in the visible changes invalidates them. The new text says that with the coordinator connection down, a drain with no unfinished work waits 10 seconds and then finishes without a coordinator acknowledgement. The text claims the disconnect already cancelled accepted work, so I see no stale authorization or credential-custody weakening in the documented behavior. The 15 s per-model unload timeout, after which a stuck native retirement is left to process exit, is an availability and lifecycle statement and does not touch plaintext handling. The claim that T-028 residual GPU data is unaffected is not verified, because `unloadAllModelsForShutdown` is not in the supplied evidence.

Open question for integration: whether the documented behavior matches the code (`ProviderLoop.unloadAllModelsForShutdown`, `ServiceDrain`). That code was not supplied, so nothing here is a finding. No new attack surface or documentation drift against the threat model is evident from the visible text. I could not view the truncated patch, so remaining hunk content is unverified.
